about: Server-side state of ls::anubis::System while it restores Anubis (behaviour script) trees from a savegame: the SavegameVisitor taken from ls::anubis::LoadRequestOneFrameComponent, an ls::anubis::savegame::Reader over the saved data, a set of entities and two flags. Seen in the same step as LoadRequestOneFrameComponent (level change through S_CTY_LevelSwapTeleporter_WYR).

evidence.says: bg3.exe+0x3839D90 (add helper, size 0xE8) copies param+0 first; live value equals ls::anubis::LoadRequestOneFrameComponent's SavegameVisitor* (stored by bg3.exe+0x2B1D4B0, esv::SessionLoadSystem)
macOS ~LoadingComponent calls ls::anubis::savegame::Reader::~Reader(this+8); Windows bg3.exe+0x3839D90 moves +8..+0xA0 with bg3.exe+0x3828430 (0x98 bytes)

macOS ~LoadingComponent: HashTable<ls::ID<ecs::EntityHandleTraits>, ls::anubis::AnubisHashTableOps>::~HashTable(this+0xA0); Windows bg3.exe+0x3839D90 moves three ptr/u32/u32 groups at +0xA0/+0xB0/+0xC0; live: bucket count 0x35, next-ids 0x20/0x20, keys 0x20/0x20 - the ls::HashSet shape
macOS ~LoadingComponent frees the pointer at +0xD0; Windows moves ptr/u32/u32 at +0xD0; live heap, capacity 0x20, size 0; element type not established
bg3.exe+0x3839D90 copies one byte at +0xE0; live 0
bg3.exe+0x3839D90 copies one byte at +0xE1; live 1
never copied by the move; live garbage

open_questions: element types of the Reader's arrays and of the array at +0xD0 (declared as raw ptr/capacity/size)
meaning of the two flags at +0xE0/+0xE1
is AnubisHashTableOps' HashTable exactly ls::HashSet (shape matches live)
survey.raw_check: 3 instances, se-fork/coverage/check.py raw stage, game v4.76.31.656

fields.name: Buf
fields.evidence: pointer half of an ls::Array (moved and zeroed together with the two counters)

fields.name: Registry
fields.evidence: Reader +0. ls::anubis::savegame::Writer::Writer(Registry&) (AnubisFramework.dll+0x105AF0) stores '*(Registry**)this = param_1' before constructing the Header at +8; macOS Reader::Reader(Writer&&) (bg3_macos_x64+0x6740F00) copies Writer +0 to Reader +0 first.

fields.name: Scalars
fields.evidence: Reader +8 is model::Header (macOS Reader::Reader(Writer&&) moves Writer +8..+0x78 member for member); this is Header +0. AnubisFramework.dll+0x1196D0 ls::anubis::savegame::model::Header::Visit visits the Header's seven arrays in order with keys built from string literals: +0 'Scalar' (DAT_1801b0e38, init AnubisFramework.dll+0x15E50), +0x10 'Table' (+0x16090), +0x20 'TableEntry' (+0x160C0), +0x30 'Variable', +0x40 tree key, +0x50 'Operation', +0x60 'Component' - the last four match the arrays already named Variables / Trees / Operations / Components from macOS Header::~Header (bg3_macos_x64+0x667E5F0).
